runs.question: How does the NIST Generative AI Profile describe data privacy risks?

answer.text:
The retrieved passages don't include the section of the NIST Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1) that covers data privacy risks, so I can't describe how it treats them.

The passages do show what the Profile covers in general. It is described as a profile of the AI RMF elaborating risks unique to or exacerbated by generative AI and how to apply the AI RMF to manage them. Another NIST report notes that the Profile highlights twelve different categories of risk from generative AI in more detail. The passages don't list those twelve categories, so I can't say whether privacy is one of them.

The retrieved passages do discuss privacy in the base framework, NIST AI 100-1 (AI RMF 1.0), not the Generative AI Profile. That framework says AI systems can also present new risks to privacy by allowing inference to identify individuals or previously private information about individuals. It also says privacy-related risks may influence security, bias, and transparency and come with tradeoffs with these other characteristics. This is general AI RMF guidance and may not reflect how the Generative AI Profile addresses privacy.

To answer your question, the Generative AI Profile's privacy section would need to be retrieved.
